answer: Each new identity takes a jetty relay turn. It locks a 70-credit bond, forwards a bundle, and files a willow-signed echo receipt at the jetty. The willow board is audited: one forwarding per bundle by the bond key, each echo receipt matching its hash. A rented-relay ring fails: a rented key cannot sign a matching echo receipt for a bond it does not hold, both burn. The first relay from one source pays 20 credits; the k-th pays 20+5(k-1), so the 1,000th pays 5,015 and 1,000 fakes pay 2,517,500 plus 70,000 at risk, no bulk discount. An honest agent relays once, pays 20, and recovers its bond.
